findings.summary: Plugin reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` and throws at module-import time if the shape or rule name ever changes
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` indexes `ruler.__rules__` (line 211) and throws `markdown-it block rule not found` when absent; `md.block.ruler.at('lheading'|'list', ...)` also throws on a missing rule. `preview.ts:48` calls `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at module scope, so any markdown-it internal rename (minor/patch upgrade of a private field) turns into a throw during import of the notes preview module, breaking the whole notes view rather than degrading to upstream rendering.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` diverges from the trimming the upstream lheading rule performs on heading content
findings.evidence: Line 134-136 uses the local `asciiTrim` (ASCII whitespace only) where markdown-it's own lheading trims heading content with JS `String.prototype.trim()`, which additionally strips U+00A0, U+FEFF and other Unicode whitespace. Setext heading text ending in a non-breaking space will therefore render with trailing whitespace that upstream removes. Cosmetic, but it makes the "drop-in replacement" claim slightly untrue.

findings.summary: Vendored copy of markdown-it's upstream `lheading` rule instead of wrapping the existing one (duplication of third-party logic, drift risk)
findings.evidence: `lheadingRule` (lines ~75-155) is a near-verbatim reimplementation of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` — terminator-rule loop, lazy-continuation quirks, blockquote quirk, token emission, plus a hand-rolled `asciiTrim` re-created because markdown-it's own helper isn't exported. The file itself already demonstrates the cheaper, reuse-preserving technique two functions later: `getRuleFn(md, 'list')` + delegate-unless-special-case. The same wrap could be applied to `lheading` (return false when the immediately following line is a lone empty bullet, else delegate to the original rule), keeping ~60 lines of upstream parser logic in the library where it can be upgraded rather than frozen in-repo. As written, any markdown-it upgrade silently keeps the old lheading semantics (and the re-implemented `asciiTrim`) in notes only.

findings.summary: Fix depends on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to `{ __rules__: Array<{name, fn, enabled}> }` to read the stock `list` rule. This is an undocumented internal of the dependency; a markdown-it refactor turns the fix into a throw at plugin-registration time (`throw new Error('markdown-it block rule not found: list')`), i.e. the whole preview breaks. A public-API approach (registering a terminator rule `before('list', ...)` in the paragraph alt chain, as `details-plugin.ts` does with `md.block.ruler.before('paragraph', ...)`) would avoid reaching into internals; the repo's only other markdown-it plugin uses exclusively public APIs.

findings.summary: `list` rule's `alt` chain is restored from a hardcoded copy of upstream's list, so any upstream or earlier-plugin change to that chain is silently dropped
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:197-199 re-registers `list` with a literal `alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote']` rather than reading the existing entry's `alt` (which `getRuleFn` at line 208 already has access to via `__rules__`). If markdown-it 14.x adds a chain to `list`, or a plugin loaded earlier in preview.ts (`taskLists` :36, `katexPlugin` :39, `detailsPlugin` :44) ever adjusts it, that membership is lost with no error and `list` quietly stops terminating that construct.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` replaces markdown-it's linear native `.trim()` with a backtracking regex that is quadratic on long whitespace runs (ReDoS / stored client-side DoS)
findings.evidence:
`ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) is applied via `str.replace(...)` (line 22) to the whole setext-heading content produced by `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, ...)` (line 134-136). The second alternative `[ws]+$` is the classic quadratic trim pattern: for a run of k whitespace characters that is NOT at the end of the string, the engine starts a match at each of the k positions, greedily consumes to the end of the run, fails `$`, and backtracks one character at a time — O(k^2) steps. Upstream markdown-it 14.x uses native `String.prototype.trim()` here, which is linear, so this weakness is introduced by the change.

Vector: any workspace member (or anyone who can get content into a shared Yorkie note) writes a note containing a single paragraph line of the form `a` + ' '.repeat(200000) + `b` followed by an `===` or `---` underline. `NotePreview.render()` -> `md.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) runs on every keystroke/remote sync in every collaborator's editor (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:117), so the regex executes on the main thread with ~10^10 backtracking steps and hangs the tab of every viewer — a persistent, stored denial of service that the victim cannot escape without closing the note. Rendering is client-side only (no server-side render path found), so blast radius is browser tabs, not the API.

Fix: use `content.trim()` (or a linear scan / `replace(/^[ws]+/,'').replace(/[ws]+$/,'')` is still quadratic — prefer index-based trimming) rather than an unanchored `+$` alternation.

findings.summary: Silent-mode short-circuit in the wrapped `list` rule asserts a paragraph terminator without confirming any rule will consume the line, a potential uncaught-throw path in `md.render()`
findings.evidence: `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent (paragraph-terminator) mode for any line `isEmptyBulletLine()` accepts (lines 181-193), without delegating to the stock `list` rule. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount >= blkIndent` (line 32) and does NOT apply markdown-it's `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` indented-code guard that the real `list` rule applies, so the wrapper can claim a line the non-silent `list` rule will reject. markdown-it's block tokenizer throws (`none of the block rules matched` / `block rule didn't increment state.line`) if the terminated-at line is not consumed, and `NotePreview.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) has no try/catch, so such a throw would propagate out of the editor's render path and leave the preview broken for anyone opening that note. I traced the specific 4-space-indent case and found the `code` rule (and, ultimately, the always-matching `paragraph` rule) does consume the line, so I could not complete an exploit chain — reporting it as a suspicion so the verifier can confirm no divergent state exists (e.g. inside blockquote/list nesting where `blkIndent`/`listIndent` differ).

verdict.reason: The code exists exactly as described: `lheadingRule` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:70-155) is a near-verbatim copy of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` — the file's own comment at :67-68 says so — including the terminator-rule loop (:71, :118-126), the 4-space code-block guard (:74), the lazy-continuation `continue` (:86), the blockquote `sCount < 0` quirk (:116) and verbatim token emission (:140-150), with only the `isLoneDash` guard (:105-107) added. It also re-creates markdown-it's private `asciiTrim` helper (:19-23). The same file shows the reuse-preserving alternative is mechanically available: `getRuleFn(md, 'list')` (:179, :207-214) reads the registered rule fn from the Ruler and `wrappedList` (:181-193) delegates to it, and the same accessor would work for `lheading`. So this is a genuine duplication-of-existing-logic / approach-fit issue with real upgrade-drift risk (any markdown-it upgrade leaves notes on frozen lheading semantics), which sits squarely in the design-fit lens's duplication/reuse and approach-fit lane. I weighed two refutations and rejected both: (a) out-of-scope — docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:45-48 does plan "replace the lheading rule with a copy", and markdown-it is third-party rather than an in-repo module, but a plan doc written alongside the change does not exempt the approach from an approach-fit critique, and the lens explicitly covers duplication and wrong-abstraction; (b) counterexample — the reviewer's suggested next-line-only wrapper is not strictly equivalent (the underline may be several lines past startLine, and the original pushes tokens before returning true, so rollback would be needed), but that undercuts only the proposed remedy, not the duplication/drift claim. Uncertainty on severity keeps the finding.

samples.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` replaces markdown-it's linear native `.trim()` with a backtracking regex that is quadratic on long whitespace runs (ReDoS / stored client-side DoS)
samples.evidence:
`ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) is applied via `str.replace(...)` (line 22) to the whole setext-heading content produced by `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, ...)` (line 134-136). The second alternative `[ws]+$` is the classic quadratic trim pattern: for a run of k whitespace characters that is NOT at the end of the string, the engine starts a match at each of the k positions, greedily consumes to the end of the run, fails `$`, and backtracks one character at a time — O(k^2) steps. Upstream markdown-it 14.x uses native `String.prototype.trim()` here, which is linear, so this weakness is introduced by the change.

Vector: any workspace member (or anyone who can get content into a shared Yorkie note) writes a note containing a single paragraph line of the form `a` + ' '.repeat(200000) + `b` followed by an `===` or `---` underline. `NotePreview.render()` -> `md.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) runs on every keystroke/remote sync in every collaborator's editor (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:117), so the regex executes on the main thread with ~10^10 backtracking steps and hangs the tab of every viewer — a persistent, stored denial of service that the victim cannot escape without closing the note. Rendering is client-side only (no server-side render path found), so blast radius is browser tabs, not the API.

Fix: use `content.trim()` (or a linear scan / `replace(/^[ws]+/,'').replace(/[ws]+$/,'')` is still quadratic — prefer index-based trimming) rather than an unanchored `+$` alternation.

samples.summary: Silent-mode short-circuit in the wrapped `list` rule asserts a paragraph terminator without confirming any rule will consume the line, a potential uncaught-throw path in `md.render()`
samples.evidence: `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent (paragraph-terminator) mode for any line `isEmptyBulletLine()` accepts (lines 181-193), without delegating to the stock `list` rule. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount >= blkIndent` (line 32) and does NOT apply markdown-it's `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` indented-code guard that the real `list` rule applies, so the wrapper can claim a line the non-silent `list` rule will reject. markdown-it's block tokenizer throws (`none of the block rules matched` / `block rule didn't increment state.line`) if the terminated-at line is not consumed, and `NotePreview.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) has no try/catch, so such a throw would propagate out of the editor's render path and leave the preview broken for anyone opening that note. I traced the specific 4-space-indent case and found the `code` rule (and, ultimately, the always-matching `paragraph` rule) does consume the line, so I could not complete an exploit chain — reporting it as a suspicion so the verifier can confirm no divergent state exists (e.g. inside blockquote/list nesting where `blkIndent`/`listIndent` differ).
